The standard deviation for the distribution of sample proportions is
The theoretical standard deviation for the distribution of sample proportions is approximately
0.1179. The standard deviation from the 100 samples was 0.1237. These are close as they both
round off to 0.12 at two decimal places. This suggests that the formula for the standard
deviation given in the central limit theorem for proportions is reasonable.
We have already noted that the distribution in this case is not normal, so we have described the
center using the mean, the variation using the standard deviation, and the shape as not normal.
